card.intuition: A primary source is the thing itself — the code, the transcript, the raw log, the actual API response — not an account of it. It is expensive to load into the context window because every token bills as input, but it is complete: nothing has been pre-filtered by someone else's judgement about what mattered. Reach for it when precision matters, like the exact signature or the line that throws.
card.analogy: Auditing the ledger rather than the dashboard: the finance dashboard summarizes yesterday's numbers, but the ledger is the ground truth you pull when a specific figure matters.
card.time_complexity: The model is stateless, so a primary source loaded into context is re-read and billed on every request that needs it.
card.space_complexity: Loading a full primary source consumes the finite context window and competes with other material for attention budget.
when_to_use: When precision matters — the exact signature, the actual error, the line that throws
When an agent asserts something about behaviour, such as how retry logic backs off
When a secondary source's staleness is suspected and behaviour needs verification
gotchas: Docs, architecture diagrams, and READMEs are descriptions that drift — an agent that reads one inherits its staleness
Loading full primary sources is expensive, with every token billed as input
Completeness costs: nothing has been pre-filtered, so the source can be large and noisy

steps.label: Claim made
steps.annotation: An agent confidently states behaviour that it read out of a stale design doc.

steps.label: Locate primary source
steps.annotation: The user points the agent at the real code rather than the description of it.

steps.label: Load original
steps.annotation: The full file is loaded into context, costing tokens and competing for attention budget.

steps.label: Verify behaviour
steps.annotation: The agent reads the code itself, which is the only account that stays current with the codebase.

exercise.prompt: Complete verify_from_primary so that when the code and the doc disagree, the primary source (the code) wins over the doc's claim.
exercise.solution: verdict = 'trust the code' if code != doc_says else 'doc matches'
hints: A doc describes the code; the code is the thing itself.
When they disagree, the primary source is the current truth.
